propositions: A two-stage design (deterministic single-pass FILTER + narrowed agentic fallback) eliminates false-positive REJECTION by construction: the filter only ever PASS or ABSTAIN per criterion (never FAIL), and remaining criteria are verified by the existing agentic verifier scoped to ABSTAINED ACs.

Across 3 real closed tickets + 3 adversarial variants with planted unmet ACs, the combined filter+fallback approach consumed -26% of the agentic-only baseline's input tokens (3.14M vs 5.80M on real tickets) while achieving zero false-positive PASSes on the 5 planted unmet ACs (all ABSTAINED then FAILed).

Filter coverage is bimodal by AC style: ACs naming greppable artifacts (symbols, test functions, files) PASS from deterministic static packs (3388 story: 90% coverage); ACs asserting runtime outcomes or store-side artifacts rationally ABSTAIN, making real-ticket coverage 39% overall and savings highest for test-citing AC styles (60-80%).

The narrowing mechanism (AC-block rewrite at ticket load via mock.patch of show_ticket) integrates cleanly with the existing criteria-reduction seam and auto-narrows the agentic step budget, including epic child traversal; the 8000-character description admission cap in verify_completion is a hard constraint that kills oversized tickets deterministically.

Agentic verifier variance (±30% steps/tokens on identical criteria sets) dominates small cost deltas and produced low-rate false-FAILs on genuinely-met ACs in production runs, confirming the operator's prediction that pure single-pass verification has inherent pathology — the filter+fallback design narrows but does not eliminate this risk.
